- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope in next 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.00” values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 5 days.
